finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote code execution via Marshal.load of attacker-supplied data in POST /restore. The request parameter `state` is Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load, which instantiates arbitrary Ruby objects and runs their deserialization hooks. Code execution requires a usable gadget chain in the loaded gems; Sinatra alone does not guarantee one, so the chain is not verified here.
finding.source: app.rb:6 params[:state] (POST /restore, no authentication, no size or signature check)

trace.note: POST /restore route is defined with no auth or before-filter
params[:state] is taken from the request and base64-decoded without validation
Marshal.load deserializes the attacker bytes into arbitrary objects
state.inspect is returned to the caller, so the attacker also gets the result or an error back

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on the route. No signature or HMAC on the state. No type check on the decoded value. No allowlist of classes. Marshal.load has no safe mode. Only Base64 decoding, which is not a control.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 defines the POST /restore route with no before-filter, auth, or signature check. app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load with no type check or class allowlist. Base64 decoding is not a control. app.rb:7 returns state.inspect to the caller.
verdict.reason: The only file is app.rb, and at app.rb:5-7 an anonymous POST to /restore reaches Marshal.load on attacker-controlled bytes with no effective guard, so untrusted deserialization is confirmed. The "unauthenticated RCE" label overstates what is verified: code execution depends on a gadget chain in the loaded gems, which this repo does not show. The core finding stands, but the severity should be stated as arbitrary object instantiation with possible RCE, not confirmed RCE.
